profile.position_derivation: DERIVED, not a team sheet: mean pitch occupancy over 31 frames (3.9 s) of relative.json, oriented by the team's own centroid (depth 0.33 of the pitch, 0.16 of the half-width off centre). Under 60 s of observation this is indicative only.

derivation.body_mass_kg: ASSUMED 78 kg from published positional means for position DM. Monocular broadcast video cannot measure mass; this exists only to turn %1RM into kg.
derivation.strength_e1rm: INFERRED, NOT MEASURED. back_squat_e1rm = (1.30 + 0.80 x explosiveness/100) x body_mass = (1.30 + 0.80 x 35/100) x 78 = 122.5 kg, rounded to the 2.5 kg bar increment. The other hubs are composed from the REAL inter_hub_ratios in catalog_seed_part1.yaml (deadlift 1.20, bench 0.75, power_clean 0.68 of back squat), not re-estimated from video. Honest interval +/- 20%. Every load is prescribed as %1RM first and kg second, so the plan survives a wrong kg. Week 9 is a test week whose AMRAP replaces this inference with a measurement.
derivation.weak_stations: union of profile_effects.weak_stations over fired rules
derivation.injuries: EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION. metrics.json carries no injury history and no medical record, and computer vision cannot observe one. The upstream `injuries` field blocks whole movement patterns from selection; populating it from a screening signal would remove the exact remedial work the signal asks for (a hamstring flag would block `hinge`, deleting the RDL). Risk is expressed through profile_ext `risk_gates` instead, which caps specific nodes. The mechanism is implemented and honoured in 80_prescribe.py; the list is empty because there is no honest input for it.
derivation.level: level is not derivable from video. It is declared for the whole squad and drives deload_overdue_threshold (advanced = 4 weeks).
